span: the Court may put the defendant to terms as to costs, payment into Court or otherwise
why: Headnote paragraph on terms that may be imposed when setting aside an ex-parte decree; it neither affirms nor refuses the remedy in the visible text.

span: can be the sole basis for conviction without any corroboration
why: Court states that an authentic dying declaration that inspires confidence can alone support conviction, after being satisfied of voluntariness and credibility.

span: it is necessary to consider the evidentiary value of the dying declaration
why: Transitional sentence that introduces evaluation of the dying declaration; no position is stated.

span: once a dying declaration is found to be reliable, it can form the basis of conviction
why: Describes Shudhakar and Paniben as precedents; the current court's own adoption is not shown in this passage.

span: it was found that conviction could not be based on such dying declaration alone without corroboration
why: Describes Gopal Singh, where an infirm dying declaration needed corroboration; reported precedent, not the current court's holding.

span: There is no rule to the effect that a dying declaration is inadmissible when it is recorded by a police officer
why: Concerns admissibility of a dying declaration recorded by police, not whether it can be the sole basis for conviction.

span: dying declaration can form the sole basis for conviction
why: Court states it is well settled that a dying declaration can be the sole basis for conviction, with the caution that care is needed on its reliability.

span: a dying declaration can form basis of conviction, if in the opinion of the Court, it inspires confidence
why: Court states that a dying declaration that inspires confidence can support conviction and that one raising suspicion needs corroboration, which fits the proposition's condition of reliability.

span: it can be relied upon as the solitary piece of evidence to convict the accused
why: Headnote holding that a lawfully recorded and cogent dying declaration can alone convict; headnote confidence is capped.

span: even absence of the certificate by a Doctor is not fatal to act upon a dying declaration
why: Concerns the doctor's certificate for a dying declaration's fitness, not whether it alone can convict.

span: Corroboration is not necessary for this situation
why: Court summarises earlier decisions that an injured person's statement treated as a dying declaration needs no corroboration and can be the sole basis for conviction.
